reference.name: Best possible plan (central MILP, perfect information)

headline.text: Q-Grid lands 8.4% from the best possible plan on average; the closest alternative without a central controller, Per-building MPC (MILP), lands 9.2%; day by day, Per-building MPC (MILP) is closer on 27 of 30 days, and Q-Grid's lower mean comes from a few days with large differences (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.002).
headline.detail: Among methods that work without a central controller, Q-Grid is closest to the best possible plan on 1 of 5 campuses; elsewhere (BDG2 university site 'Fox' (Arizona); BDG2 university site 'Bull' (Texas); BDG2 university site 'Cockatoo' (New York); CU-BEMS office building, Bangkok (7 floors)) another method is closer.

step1.text: Today each building acts on its own: when BESCOM supply fails, critical loads go dark for 2.6 h per outage while the diesel sets burn 373 L; the electricity bill averages Rs 177,694 a day.

step7.text: In a BESCOM outage Q-Grid cuts critical-load downtime from 2.6 h to 55 min per outage (41 L more diesel, 110 kg CO₂, to keep those loads up); on normal days the bill is 0.4% higher and the demand charge rises by Rs 16,685 a month at 1,300 kVA contract demand; with no central controller it averages 8.4% from the best possible plan against 9.2% for Per-building MPC, a lead made on the outage days (normal days: 7.4% against 0.3%).
step7.comms: When the campus network fails for 3 hours, central control loses 2.7 points of gap and Q-Grid 0.7, because each building keeps optimising on its own.
